source.title: Scaling sparse feature circuit finding for in-context learning
source.authors: Dmitrii Kharlapenko; Stepan Shabalin; Fazl Barez; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies task-related SAE latents and feature circuits, not neuron poles or the versions' neuron-level interpretability claims. It does not test or rely on the claim that a model's own neurons are suitable units of analysis.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern SAE features and their causal roles in in-context learning. They do not measure the share of neuron poles with one or more jobs, validate explanations on held-out activations, or test neuron-based attribution graphs. The text also reports TVC method-performance results and tuning choices; those are not evidence about the claim and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyses SAE latents, transcoder features and sparse feature circuits for in-context learning in Gemma 1 2B (plus TVC on Gemma 2 and Phi-3). It reports no measure of individual neuron poles, neuron explanation scoring, or neuron-based attribution graphs. The circuits use trained SAEs/transcoders with error nodes, so they do not bear on V5's claim that neurons suffice without a replacement model. It only mentions superposition in related work. 'Discusses' fits better than 'cites_only' only loosely; it neither tests nor uses the neuron claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SAEs are valuable circuit-analysis tools for ICL in Gemma 1 2B. They identify task-execution features (decomposed from task vectors via TVC) and task-detection features that are causally linked through attention and MLP sublayers. The paper does not itself address whether individual neurons are appropriate units; the record's added contrast is an inference, not an author statement.
record.recipe_differences: The study adapts sparse feature circuit analysis and uses SAEs/transcoders and task-vector cleaning; it does not use a neuron-pole audit or neuron-based attribution graph method.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit analysis was restricted to intermediate layers 10–17 because earlier-layer IE approximations were lower quality; for the reported circuit faithfulness, focusing on layers 11–12 required around 10–60 active nodes on average. The authors also report effects varying by task and related-task grouping. Task-vector cleaning sweeps varied SAE configurations and regularization, but those results do not measure neuron interpretability shares.

fits_no_version.finding: Executor SAE features put 89.8% of activation mass on arrow tokens; detector features put 96.76% on output tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Gemma 1 2B, task-execution and task-detection SAE features activate at distinct token positions in ICL prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-feature circuits of 500 nodes reached average faithfulness 0.6; restricting to layers 11–12 needed about 10–60 nodes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse SAE-feature circuits preserve much of ICL task performance in Gemma 1 2B, with size depending on layer range.

fits_no_version.finding: Circuit ablations and detector ablations were mostly task-specific, with weaker detector-executor links for person profession and present simple gerund.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-detection SAE features causally drive task-execution features, mostly task-specifically, in Gemma 1 2B.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering with single executor or detector SAE features mostly boosted only the matching task, with spillover among related tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-related SAE features have task-specific steering effects in simple ICL tasks.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says SAE training code will be made public after acceptance.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025 (as stated in the paper).
record.problems: The circuit analysis is limited to a simple task-vector setting and centers on Gemma 1 2B. The paper restricts its search to layers 10–17 and reports lower IE-approximation quality in earlier layers; it notes that SAE quality, task complexity, or token-type aggregation may affect those approximations. Some interpretability and task-specificity outcomes are described qualitatively or shown in figures rather than reported as exact values.
record.rows_left_out: No results about neuron-pole shares or the claim versions were reported. TVC-versus-baseline loss and active-feature sweeps, steering-scale selection, and other method-tuning comparisons were left out because they report method performance or tuning rather than neuron interpretability.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit shares; not studied.
Neuron-pole shares across models and scales; SAE features only.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, recursive generalization; no vision models.
Neuron interpretability rates versus architecture or tools; not measured.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model; the study uses SAE/transcoder circuits instead and reports no neuron-circuit comparison.
Held-out prediction of neuron firing from explanations of activating examples; not done (only SAE max-activating examples shown).
Simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations; not done.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The study's framing (SAEs address superposition) implicitly sits opposite the essay's thesis, but it offers no neuron-level evidence, so no verdicts are given. R17's 'partial' state concerns detector-execution coupling, not any version.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole shares and the Qwen3-32B audit.
Shares of interpretable neuron poles across models, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, and recursive generalization.
Neuron interpretability rates, architectural causes, and the InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
Attribution graphs built from model neurons and comparison with a trained replacement model or its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict firing on new activations.
Automated explanation scores from simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Gemma 1 2B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated nodes in the complement of the discovered task circuits and measured task-performance degradation.
rows.measure: Faithfulness of the complement; task-performance degradation
rows.baseline: Complete-model performance and empty-circuit baseline define the faithfulness measure
rows.value: Several hundred features were needed to achieve degradation similar to complex cases in the SFC paper; no exact value stated.
rows.note: The description gives no exact faithfulness value for the complement.

rows.subject: Gemma 1 2B

rows.subject: Gemma 1 2B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the highest-IE nodes for one task until its faithfulness dropped to 0.3, then measured effects on other tasks.
rows.baseline: Faithfulness before ablation; exact values not stated
rows.value: Degradation was largely confined to the target task; exceptions were closely related tasks, including translation pairs and person language/location language.
rows.note: The paper describes the cross-task results qualitatively.

rows.subject: Gemma 1 2B
rows.operation_detail: Steered zero-shot prompts with individual task-execution SAE features and measured relative loss improvement.

conditions.value: diverse task set; results aggregated in heatmap

rows.measure: Task loss effect and task specificity
rows.value: Most features with a high effect on one task generally did not significantly affect unrelated tasks; related-task features sometimes affected tasks in the same group.
rows.note: The paper reports this as an aggregate description of the heatmap.

conditions.value: diverse task set; results aggregated in heatmap

rows.measure: Task loss effect and task specificity

rows.note: The paper reports this as an aggregate description of the heatmap.

rows.subject: Gemma 1 2B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated task-detection directions while fixing attention patterns and measured corresponding task-execution-feature activations.

conditions.value: matched strongest detection and execution features by task

rows.baseline: Activation without detection-direction ablation; exact values not stated
rows.value: Ablating detection features substantially reduced activation of corresponding execution features; person profession and present simple gerund showed unusually weak connections.
rows.note: The paper describes the reduction as substantial overall and identifies two weaker task connections.
